notes: Factor ratings (0-10) are editorial judgments applied uniformly to every entry by one rubric. Critical Read is scored from the critical consensus alone, identically for all entries. Crowd star ratings are rounded aggregates observed on review platforms at the dataset version shown; they are displayed as context and are not scored. Locations marked verified were read from the pizzeria's own site on the date recorded.

restaurants.name: Windy City Pie
restaurants.signature: The caramelized cheese crown — a molten parmesan ring fused to the pan wall
restaurants.blurb: Started as a clandestine SoDo parking-lot handoff: call ahead, text on arrival, trade cash for a deep pan pie. Now a proper Phinney Ridge dining room where your pizza is walked to the table like a bottle of Barolo. The bake is engineered — a buttery biscuit-crumb base, a tomato layer with real acid, and a cheese wall that shatters.

restaurants.name: Delancey
restaurants.signature: Long-fermented Washington wheat dough, blistered and pliant
restaurants.blurb: The pie that recalibrated Seattle's expectations in 2009 and still sets the floor for everyone else. Brandon Pettit's dough ferments for days on local wheat, then goes into a wood oven that leaves leopard char without sacrificing the fold. The crocodile-hide underside is the whole argument.

restaurants.name: Cornelly
restaurants.signature: Seasonal produce treated as the main event, not a garnish
restaurants.blurb: The Delancey brain trust pointed at the farmers market. Pizza is the backbone but the kitchen behaves like a full restaurant — charred brassicas, whipped ricotta, whatever the week gave them. It is the most convincing case in the city that a pizzeria can also be a serious vegetable restaurant.

locations.address: 2121 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA 98109

restaurants.name: Moto Pizza
restaurants.signature: A 72-hour dough baked into a crisp-edged slab with absurd topping architecture
restaurants.blurb: The hardest reservation in Seattle pizza and it isn't close — drops sell out in minutes and the waitlist has become part of the folklore. What arrives justifies more of the hype than it has any right to: a tall, airy, crunchy-bottomed pan pie built with real precision.

restaurants.name: Serious Pie
restaurants.style: Blistered thin crust, applewood stone oven
restaurants.signature: Sweet fennel sausage and roasted peppers on a charred, cracker-edged base
restaurants.blurb: Tom Douglas's applewood-fired room has been packing communal tables since 2006 and remains the most reliable pizza in the core. The crust runs thin and aggressively blistered; the topping list stays short and Pacific Northwest-literate. Still the default answer when someone visiting asks.

restaurants.name: Dino's Tomato Pie
restaurants.signature: Sauce-on-top square slices under a red neon glow
restaurants.blurb: A love letter to New Jersey pizza parlors, right down to the bar-forward room and the sauce ladled over the cheese. The squares are thin, crackly and built for a beer at 11pm. Nothing else in Seattle is doing this style with this much conviction.

restaurants.name: Lupo
restaurants.signature: Sourdough base with a menu that turns over with the market
restaurants.blurb: A small, tightly-run room where the dough is naturally leavened and the toppings change on the kitchen's whim. The bake sits in the sweet spot between Neapolitan softness and a crust with actual structure — you can pick up a slice without it surrendering.

restaurants.name: The Independent Pizzeria
restaurants.signature: A tiny wood oven and a menu that refuses to grow
restaurants.blurb: Barely bigger than a living room, a few blocks from Lake Washington. The wood oven runs hot, the pies come out fast and thin, and the whole operation is an argument for doing one thing at a scale you can actually control. Long a critics' quiet favorite.

restaurants.name: Tutta Bella
restaurants.signature: Verace Pizza Napoletana certification — 90 seconds at 900°F
restaurants.blurb: Washington's first VPN-certified pizzeria and the reason a generation of Seattleites knows what a true Neapolitan pie is supposed to taste like. It is textbook by design: soppressata piccante, San Marzano, fior di latte, a soft and soupy center. Consistent across every location, which is its own achievement.

locations.address: 15600 NE 8th St., Suite J1, Bellevue, WA 98008

restaurants.name: Pagliacci Pizza
restaurants.signature: The Primo Gusto slice, available approximately everywhere, forever
restaurants.blurb: The civic baseline. Since 1979 Pagliacci has been the pizza Seattle actually eats — a reliable slice on a corner in nearly every neighborhood, seasonal specials that are better than they need to be, and a delivery operation that borders on infrastructure. Not the city's best pie. Comfortably its most important.

locations.address: 6224 Sand Point Way NE, Seattle, WA 98115

restaurants.name: Breezy Town Pizza
restaurants.signature: A sourdough deep-dish served out of the back of a dive bar
restaurants.blurb: Windy City Pie's sibling, operating inside the Clock-Out Lounge. Same engineered pan bake, same caramelised cheese edge, but with a sourdough base and a room where a punk show might be starting. The most promising promotion candidate on the bench.

restaurants.name: Via Tribunali
restaurants.signature: Wood-fired Neapolitan from imported ovens, unchanged for two decades
restaurants.blurb: One of the city's original Neapolitan rooms, dark and wood-fired and stubbornly consistent. Where Tutta Bella made the style legible to Seattle, Via Tribunali kept it moody and Italian.

restaurants.name: Big Mario's
restaurants.signature: A foldable 18-inch pepperoni slice at one in the morning
restaurants.blurb: The default Capitol Hill late-night slice, and a genuinely good New York pie rather than a merely convenient one. Thin, foldable, greasy in the correct way.

restaurants.name: Flying Squirrel Pizza
restaurants.signature: Mixtape-named pies built on organic Northwest produce
restaurants.blurb: A neighbourhood parlour that treats the topping list as a place to have ideas, using organic ingredients without making a religion of it. Cosy, unpretentious and reliably interesting.
restaurants.statusNote: The last remaining Flying Squirrel Pizza location, in Georgetown, closed for good on March 1, 2024 after a decade in business, with no relocation.

restaurants.name: Proletariat Pizza
restaurants.signature: A White Center institution that never chased the city's attention
restaurants.blurb: Unfussy, generous and beloved locally in a way the downtown lists rarely register. The kind of place that anchors a neighbourhood rather than a listicle.

restaurants.name: Ballard Pizza Company
restaurants.signature: Ethan Stowell's slice shop, run with restaurant discipline
restaurants.blurb: A chef-driven take on the counter slice: better sourcing than the format demands, executed at volume. Proof that a slice shop can be serious without being precious.

restaurants.name: Zeeks Pizza
restaurants.signature: Toppings that have no business working, and mostly do
restaurants.blurb: A local chain that built its identity on combinations other kitchens would refuse. Not the city's best crust, but a genuine Seattle institution with more conviction than its size suggests.

locations.address: 7900 E Greenlake Drive N, Seattle, WA 98103
1915 Queen Anne Ave. N, Seattle, WA 98109
24015 Van Ry Blvd, Mountlake Terrace, WA 98043

restaurants.name: Talarico's
restaurants.signature: A slice the size of a dinner plate, sold by the single
restaurants.blurb: West Seattle's answer to the late-night question, famous for slices that genuinely require two hands. The spectacle is the point, but the pie underneath holds up.

restaurants.name: Hot Mama's Pizza
restaurants.signature: The cheapest honest slice on Pike/Pine
restaurants.blurb: No ambition beyond feeding Capitol Hill quickly and cheaply, executed without cynicism. The value benchmark every other slice in the city is measured against.

restaurants.name: Humble Pie
restaurants.signature: Wood-fired pies eaten at picnic tables beside the garden they came from
restaurants.blurb: A walled garden, a wood oven and a menu that leans on what is growing outside. More an argument about how to eat pizza than a competitor on crust alone.

restaurants.name: Pizzeria Gabbiano
restaurants.signature: Roman thin-crust and sandwiches in a corner of Pioneer Square
restaurants.blurb: The only kitchen in the city making a serious case for the Roman style — crisper, flatter and drier than the Neapolitan orthodoxy that surrounds it.
restaurants.statusNote: Closed in 2016; the Pioneer Square space became Il Corvo Pasta Studio.

restaurants.name: Post Alley Pizza
restaurants.signature: A counter slice in the middle of the market crowds
restaurants.blurb: Geography is half the appeal, but the pie is better than a tourist corridor requires. A reliable slice in the one part of town where that is hardest to find.

restaurants.name: Pegasus Pizza
restaurants.signature: Pizza with a view of the water and forty years of regulars
restaurants.blurb: An Alki institution where the setting and the sunset do real work. Recently changed hands, which makes its next year worth watching closely.

restaurants.name: Slice Box
restaurants.signature: Pies that treat the format as a canvas rather than a tradition
restaurants.blurb: Georgetown-appropriate: weird on purpose, occasionally brilliant, never boring. The bench entry most likely to either climb sharply or stay exactly where it is.

restaurants.name: Rocco's
restaurants.signature: A slice and a beer at closing time in Belltown
restaurants.blurb: Belltown's late-night anchor, doing volume without the pie collapsing into an afterthought. The bar is the draw; the pizza is why you stay.

restaurants.name: My Friend Derek's
restaurants.blurb: A home-oven pop-up that sold out most nights has grown into a permanent Tangletown storefront, still built around the same wood-fired thin crust.
restaurants.statusNote: The Detroit-style pop-up converted to a permanent brick-and-mortar in Tangletown and is now operating with regular weekly hours.

craft.note: The Infatuation scored it 8.8/10, praising 'sturdy-but-light caramelized crusts' and calling the plain Detroit-style pie 'sublime,' alongside inventive slices like a Fishy Caesar; a Seattle pizza-focused newsletter ranked it #3 in its Definitive Seattle Pizza Rankings.

restaurants.name: Abecedary
restaurants.blurb: Pizzaiolo Seth Eisner gave Seattle a cheese-and-basil sneak preview at the Hillman City Block Party; the full New Haven-style pizzeria and brewery isn't slated to open until 2027.

restaurants.name: Stevie's Famous
restaurants.blurb: Burien-founded, Seattle Times reader-poll pizzeria that opened its first Seattle-proper flagship in the former Zeek's Pizza space on Phinney Ave N in July 2026.

mentions.title: Opening Night: Stevie's Famous Comes to North Seattle

craft.note: The Seattle Times called the original location worth a 'pizza pilgrimage' for its burrata-and-hot-honey pies on a 'crispy, never burned crust' and later crowned it champion of its citywide Pizza Smackdown; the Phinney Ridge location, opened in 2026, is now the flagship producing dough for all locations, and The Infatuation confirms it serves 'the same burrata-dolloped pies.'

restaurants.name: Sinners Pizza
restaurants.blurb: Heaven-and-Hell-themed late-night New York-style pizza shop and bar that opened April 10, 2026 on the Ave in the former Supreme Pizzeria & Bar space.

restaurants.name: Roma Roma
restaurants.blurb: Brothers Forrest and Colin Brunton's Roman-style by-the-cut pizza counter, priced by weight, that opened on 12th Ave in the former Rachel's Ginger Beer space.

restaurants.name: Pizza By Ruffin
restaurants.blurb: Washington's first Black-owned pizzeria, serving Roman-style pizza al taglio with globally inspired toppings such as Jamaican curry and Ethiopian doro wat out of Fairview Market Hall.

craft.note: The Infatuation rated it 7.8/10 for its two-day cold-fermented, crackly-crust Roman al taglio slices and diaspora-inspired toppings like Jamaican-curry mushroom and gumbo-style pies; Seattle Refined covered its distinction as Washington's first Black-owned pizzeria, opened October 2024, which redirects tips to a nonprofit funding school garden grants.

restaurants.name: Cornuto Pizzeria
restaurants.blurb: Wood-fired Neapolitan-style pizzeria on Greenwood Ave N in Phinney Ridge, open Wednesday through Sunday.

craft.note: The Seattle Times called it home to 'some of the best Neapolitan-style pizza around' in a traditional white-tiled oven; The Infatuation likewise praised its 'bubbly pies drizzled with chile oil' in a cozy, narrow, date-friendly room, and PhinneyWood covered its 2016 opening in Phinney Ridge/Greenwood by brothers Andrew and Giancarlo Martino.

restaurants.name: Razzi's Pizzeria
restaurants.blurb: Long-running Greenwood pizzeria offering full gluten-free and vegan menus alongside classic Italian pizza.

craft.note: Est. 1983, Razzi's runs a certified gluten-free kitchen alongside its regular menu, with four separate allergen-safe menus that Eater's gluten-free guide calls the holy grail of allergen-safe dining; hundreds of Yelp and Tripadvisor reviews describe consistently good food and generous portions rather than standout pizza craft specifically.

restaurants.name: Pizzeria La Rocca
restaurants.blurb: Wood-fired Italian pizzeria founded in 2021 in the heart of Greenwood, using imported Italian flour and ingredients.

craft.note: Reviewers on Yelp and Tripadvisor repeatedly single out the wood-fired crust as the thinnest and most delicate they've had, calling it some of the best pizza in the Pacific Northwest; prices run higher than most Seattle neighborhood shops.

restaurants.name: Pi Vegan Pizzeria
restaurants.blurb: Seattle's 100% vegan pizzeria near the Roosevelt/University District line, with gluten-free and soy-free options.

craft.note: An all-vegan pizzeria on Roosevelt Way with a devoted following; diners on HappyCow and Yelp call the crust the star of the show and the pizza the best vegan pizza they've ever had, with affordable, budget-friendly pricing.

restaurants.name: Mioposto
restaurants.blurb: Family-owned wood-fired pizzeria, bar and Italian kitchen across from Mt. Baker park, open since 2006.

craft.note: The Seattle Times' review of the Mount Baker original describes thin, foldable crusts, ballooning edges and a bread-like chew, tracing owner Jeremy Hardy's pizza pedigree through Pizzeria Bianco, dough school, and time in Florence and Rome; Seattle Met has carried it on its business listings since it opened in 2006.

restaurants.name: Veraci Pizza
restaurants.blurb: Wood-fired artisan pizzeria that grew out of a Ballard Farmers Market oven, now with a standalone Wedgwood location.

craft.note: Fearless Critic scores Veraci's Neapolitan-style, applewood-fired slices 7.5/10 for food, tying for fifth among Seattle pizzerias at roughly $25 a person; the business grew out of a mobile wood-fired oven the founders built to sell pizza at the Ballard Farmers Market starting in 2004.

restaurants.name: South Town Pie
restaurants.blurb: New York-style pizza bar in South Park from chef Sam Crannell (formerly of LloydMartin), with a full bar, outdoor seating and pinball machines.

craft.note: The Infatuation rated it 7.4/10, saying the New York-style pizza has grown inconsistent since its early days — standard red-sauced pies now read as 'underseasoned' — but singled out the pastrami pie (everything-bagel-spiced crust, gruyere fondue, caramelized onion, pickles) as the one order that 'has stood the test of time beautifully.' It's a casual pizza-and-bar room in South Park from chef Sam Crannell, formerly of LloydMartin, with a creative menu that also runs to a breakfast pie and a wild boar ragu pie with fried sage and Funyuns.

restaurants.name: Pizzeria 22
restaurants.blurb: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria in West Seattle's Admiral district serving Margherita D.O.C. and a weekend wood-fired brunch.

craft.note: Seattle magazine praised the 'sturdy, chewy-crusted' wood-fired pies at this Admiral District spot from owner Cary Kemp, who trained at Sorbillo in Naples; the review calls out buffalo mozzarella added midway through the bake to protect the crust, house-sliced prosciutto, and a wood-oven clam special served with blistered, Parmesan-dusted flatbread. It is West Seattle's only VPN-certified Neapolitan kitchen, running an imported wood oven and Italian '00' flour and San Marzano-style tomatoes.

restaurants.name: Johnny Mo's Pizzeria
restaurants.blurb: Chicago-style deep-dish pizzeria that started in a small nook in Eastlake and also serves a Chicago-style slice.

locations.address: 3272 Fuhrman Ave E, Suite 100, Seattle, WA 98102

craft.note: Seattle Met's comparison of the shop's dual New York and Chicago pies found the thin, foldable New York slice 'wins on both texture and wait times' against the 30-minute deep dish -- a well-executed neighborhood two-style shop rather than a destination for either style alone.

restaurants.name: Pazzo's on Eastlake
restaurants.blurb: Neighborhood pizza-and-bar spot on Eastlake Ave E with a dining room, lounge and seasonal patio.

craft.note: A 1992 Seattle Times review of this Eastlake stone-oven pizzeria called pies like the Pazzo Pollo and the Prato excellent to very good, while flagging an underbaked crust on the Milano and an overloaded, unrestrained topping combo on the Bari -- a mixed-but-solid picture consistent with its decades-long run as a neighborhood institution where calzones outsell the pizza.

restaurants.name: Soprano's Antico
restaurants.blurb: Family-run pizza and pasta restaurant in the Admiral Junction making house-made dough and pasta daily.

craft.note: West Seattle Herald and West Seattle Blog coverage of its long-delayed 2017 opening describe owner Plamen Stoyanov's Neapolitan program -- San Marzano tomatoes, Caputo flour, buffalo mozzarella -- built on training and certification under 12-time world pizza champion Tony Gemignani.

restaurants.name: Pizza Ritual
restaurants.blurb: Takeout-only pop-up-turned-permanent pizzeria running out of the KBM Kitchen walk-up window, serving naturally leavened Neapolitan-style pizza Friday and Saturday evenings.

craft.note: The Infatuation (7.8/10) praises this Delridge takeout window's naturally leavened, long-fermented pies for charred, bubbled crusts and bold tang, calling it a fix for a Neapolitan-shaped hole in West Seattle, while noting not every topping combo lands.

restaurants.blurb: Long-running wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria on Rainier Ave S, marked by a red glowing 'Wood Fire Pizza' sign, serving margherita pies and pasta.

craft.note: Seattle Times critic Providence Cicero gave Pulcinella three stars for VPN-certified true Neapolitan pizza baked in about 90 seconds in an imported Valoriani wood oven; The Infatuation still sends readers to Rainier Beach for a margherita well above heat-lamp-slice territory.

restaurants.name: Romano Pizza & Pasta
restaurants.blurb: Long-running Delridge pizza-and-pasta shop (formerly Olympia Pizza & Pasta) also serving calzones and Greek specialties.

restaurants.name: World Pizza
restaurants.blurb: All-vegetarian pizza shop that has served the Chinatown-International District since reopening at this King Street location in 2011, after starting in Belltown in the 1990s.

craft.note: A Chinatown-ID fixture since opening in Belltown in 1992 (relocated to King St in 2011), World Pizza is one of the city's few vegetarian-only slice shops, cited by Thrillist and Seattle Metropolitan for inventive toppings like gorgonzola-potato-rosemary on an unfussy, utilitarian crust.

restaurants.name: Sacro Bosco Pizza & Wine
restaurants.blurb: Pizza-and-wine service run by the Temple Pastries bakery team, known for massive crunchy-yet-airy Roman-style rectangles.

restaurants.name: Oxbow
restaurants.style: Bakery counter, offbeat whole pies and slices
restaurants.blurb: Sea Wolf-affiliated bakery and bagel shop that has also served whole pies and slices from noon to 5pm daily since opening in 2022.

craft.note: The Infatuation calls the pizza Oxbow's finest asset -- a scientifically precise, crunchy-bottomed crust with an inflated cornicione, topped with inventive, seasonally rotating combinations like chimichurri-scallion-cotija and bacon-crackling pepperoni; the Seattle Times covered its 2022 opening as one of the city's notable new pizza launches, from the Sea Wolf bakery team's fermented-starter dough.

restaurants.name: A Pizza Mart (First Hill)
restaurants.blurb: Independent Seattle slice shop on Seneca Street serving First Hill, part of the locally owned A Pizza Mart mini-chain.
